messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Evaluate code but do not markup
messages.body_plain:
I guess the easiest approach might be to write the output to a
temporary file or stdout(), e.g. knit('foo.Rmd', output = tempfile()).
Constructing the output markup is relatively cheap compared to
executing the R code chunks, so it may not be a bad idea to do it and
discard it.

Note that child documents do not produce file output -- only character
strings of the markup are returned, e.g. this will not produce
child-a.md if you put this child chunk in a main document:

```{r child='child-a.Rmd'}
```

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain: Alex, Ah, thanks for clarifying. If knitr isn't generating the image, than of course any knitr settings have no effect. It's important to keep in mind what tools are doing what. Knitr is not a markdown parser, it isn't touching your markdown. It's just turning your R code chunks into the desired output (in this case, markdown). When knitr sees some markdown code like ![](/path/to/my_image.png) it just leaves it as is, because it's not an R chunk. Just like any other markdown text. Does that make sense? So then of course the image_uri setting has no effect. Pandoc, unlike knitr, is a markdown parser, so it reads all the markdown. Sounds like all you need is to convert your existing, non-knitr generated images to base64. You can do that in R, e.g. by using the function that knitr is using in image_uri (markdown:::.b64EncodeFile, or just copy-paste the data-uris generated by pandoc back into your markdown). messages.subject: Reusing figures for multiple output formats?
messages.subject_clean: Reusing figures for multiple output formats?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Does anyone happen to know of a way to generate a figure once, and reuse the output for multiple output formats?

By using the caching feature of knitr, it's possible to avoid rerunning computationally-intensive bits of code when outputting to multiple formats, however, plots are typically still created anew for each additional format, which can take a long time.

The main two formats I'm interested in outputting to at the moment are HTML and PDF and I am using rmarkdown to handle the conversion. I've tried setting dev='png' to force the PDF output to use PNG, but it ends up generating a second version of the PNG in a different sub-directory (figure-html and figure-latex). I also tried setting dev to both "pdf" and "png", but this also does not solve the issue.

Here is an example .Rmd file to demonstrate the issue:

> ---
> output: [html_document, pdf_document]
> ---
>
> Test
> ====
>
> To reproduce:
>
> > library(rmarkdown)
> > render('knitr_multiple_formats.rmd', output_format='all')
>
> ```{r knitr_settings, include=FALSE}
> library(knitr)
> opts_chunk$set(dev='png')
> ```
>
> ```{r block1, cache=TRUE}
> x = matrix(rnorm(1500^2), ncol=1500)
> hist(x)
> ```
>
> ```{r block2, cache=TRUE}
> library(gplots)
>
> t1 = Sys.time()
> heatmap.2(x, trace='none')
> t2 = Sys.time()
>
> print(t2 - t1)
> ```

When the above example, it only takes a minute or so to generate each copy of the plot, however, you as the size of the data matrix grows, the added burden of regenerating the plot becomes significant.

Anyone know of a way around this?

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Cheers,
Keith

solution, but it will assign each output format a separate cache
directory, so that the cache is not invalidated when you switch
between output formats. Note, however, the code chunk has to be
executed for each output format for at least once.

Yihui

Hello. After I got the email about the new changes in knitr 1.6 I tried using rmarkdown to build my vignette instead of knitr, and the size of the .html documentation went from 1.3MB to 4.8MB. This sets off notes when checking the package for CRAN.

I.e., using:

<!--
%\VignetteEngine{knitr::knitr}
%\VignetteIndexEntry{Intro to the qqman package}
-->

My vignette .html file is 1.3MB.

Using:

<!--
%\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
%\VignetteIndexEntry{Intro to the qqman package}
-->

My vignette is 4.8MB, and I get NOTEs on the build/check process. CRAN's policy dictates no package should be over 5MB, and this sets me over that limit. I like the formatting I get with rmarkdown. Any ideas how to reduce the size?

The example HTML file produced by this is here on github. It seems to be the PNG image data, but I'm not sure how to fix this short of getting rid of the images produced.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stephenturner/qqman/dev/inst/doc/qqman.html

Thanks,

Stephen

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Vignette created with knitr 1.6 and rmarkdown is 4x larger in size
messages.body_plain:
By default, the HTML document format of rmarkdown uses high resolution
graphics by 1) increasing the default dpi from 72 to 96, and 2)
doubling the physical image size and halving the display size so that
the plots can make use of the Retina Display if available (this is set
by the chunk option fig.retina = 2). You can see how these chunk
options are set in rmarkdown:
https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/R/html_document.R

This will certainly increase the size of .html vignettes, so I guess
you can revert to the old chunk options to make CRAN happy:
opts_chunk$set(dpi = 72, fig.retina = 1)

Regards,
Yihui
--
